subject: Post-call recap: TCO summary & next steps (token economics, batching/caching)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: TCO summary & next steps (token economics, batching/caching)

John — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a proposed next steps checklist so we can move this toward procurement.

Pain points we heard
- High per-token costs for large-document summarization and conversational search (current spend spikes on peak hours).
- Large variance in latency under bursty traffic (affects UX for customer-facing features).
- Internal compliance requirement to keep logs 6 months and strict data isolation for PII.

Goals you shared
- Reduce monthly spend on LLM inference by ~30% while keeping quality within 5% of current outputs.
- Get latency under 300ms p95 for 75% of conversational traffic.
- Pilot with a single product line (Support Summaries) in Q1.

TCO levers we discussed (high level)
- Token economics: current model usage profile you provided (~10B tokens/month across prompts + completions). At our hosted API baseline, this maps to an estimated $X/month (see attached snapshot).
- Batching & continuous KV caching: for your workload we estimate 20–35% token-cost savings by enabling batching on batched inference paths and reusing KV cache for repeated session context.
- Model variants & quantization: using a 4-bit quantized performance tier for non-sensitive workloads can reduce compute cost ~25% with negligible quality drop on NLU tasks.
- Smart routing: route low-latency critical calls to a fast (higher-cost) pool and bulk async jobs to cheaper capacity. Estimated blended savings in attached TCO.

Immediate next steps
1) I attached a preliminary ACME-TCO-Snapshot.xlsx with assumptions used today. Please review the input columns (tokens/month, avg prompt length, percent cached).
2) Rafael will follow up with a short config proposal for batching + KV settings tailored to Support Summaries.
3) If the numbers look, we can set up a technical pilot: 2-week pilot on a dedicated pool (discounted pilot pricing) to validate latency & cost.

Would you be able to confirm the tokens/month figure in tab A of the spreadsheet (there's a highlighted cell)? If yes, we can lock pilot dates next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Attachments: ACME-TCO-Snapshot.xlsx, redwood-pricing.pdf

From: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: TCO summary & next steps (token economics, batching/caching)

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary and good alignment on levers. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Tokens/month: the 10B is a blended estimate. For Support Summaries specifically it's ~1.2B/month (we highlighted that in cell B6). The rest is background batch jobs (search indexing) that we may migrate later.
- Budget constraint: procurement signaled a $35k/month target for the pilot phase (this is soft but useful context).
- Compliance: PII redaction is mandatory — any KV caching or session reuse must be configurable to strip PII before cache write.

Agree with the pilot approach. Procurement wants a simple 2-week cost validation report (actual vs estimate) and a short SOW. Can Rafael and your pricing team include a line showing worst-case spend if batching doesn't reach the expected 20% savings? That will make procurement comfortable.

I'll review the snapshot and confirm the highlighted token cell today. Please include me and procurement on the pilot SOW so we can fast-track.

—John
Head of Product, Acme Corp
john.doe@acmecorp.com | +1 617-555-0102

John — great, thanks for the clarifications and the procurement budget signal. Quick follow-up commitments from our side: 

- Rafael will send the pilot config + worst-case spend scenario by EOD today. (Rafael: ping)
- I'll update the ACME-TCO-Snapshot.xlsx to split Support Summaries vs background jobs and add a "worst-case" column that assumes no batching gains.
- On PII/Compliance: our KV cache has hooks for pre-write transformers; we can add a PII redaction step before caching or skip cache for PII-containing flows. We'll include that in SOW language.

Proposed next meeting: 30-minute alignment call with procurement + Rafael + Priyom on Friday 10 Dec at 10:00 AM PT to review the SOW and pilot pricing. Does that work for you?

If yes, I'll send a calendar invite and the updated snapshot.

Thanks — talk soon.
Marissa
